speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: asked the Minister for Foreign Affairs what is the impact of the escalating tensions in the Middle East arising from intensified fighting along Lebanon’s southern border and Hezbollah’s increasing use of reconnaissance drones over northern Israel, for Singapore.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: asked the Minister for Foreign Affairs how is Singapore, together with the international community, playing its part to ensure Israel abides by international law as it wages war against Hamas in Rafah to rescue the hostages.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I will also address the question for written answer by Member Ms Nadia Samdin in today's Order Paper, as well as questions raised by Members Mr Leong Mun Wai and Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim, which were filed for subsequent Sittings, but since it is on the same issue, I thought I would address all these questions together.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And including Question No 2 for oral answer in today's Order Paper?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We urge parties in the conflict to arrive at an agreement.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We also reiterate our call for all sides to comply with international law, including international humanitarian law.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The second point I want to make is that Singapore calls on all parties to de-escalate tensions and that there is a real and rising danger of a wider regional conflagration that needs to be avoided.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We condemn all attacks on civilians, including the recent attacks across the Israel-Lebanon border, as Mr de Souza had alluded to.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This Advisory Opinion was published on 19 July 2024.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Advisory Opinions of the ICJ carry significant weight in the international legal system and contribute to the development of international law, even though they do not in themselves create legally binding obligations.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The Advisory Opinion of 19 July 2024 that was requested by the UN General Assembly is significant.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It focuses on Israeli policies and practices in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including the issue of Israeli settlements.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres has announced that he will put the Advisory Opinion to the General Assembly to decide how to proceed in this matter.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Singapore’s long-standing position on Israeli settlements has been consistent and clear.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The settlements make it much harder to arrive at a viable two-state solution.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Singapore has consistently voted in support of UN General Assembly resolutions that reject Israeli settlement activities and call upon Israel to rescind all unilateral measures that have been taken to change the status of Jerusalem.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Singapore’s long-standing position on the Israeli-Palestinian conflict is that the only viable pathway to a comprehensive, just and durable solution is a negotiated two-state solution, consistent with all relevant UN Security Council resolutions.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And we continue to urge both parties to resume direct negotiations and to, in the meantime, refrain from unilateral actions to attempt to change the status quo because this will hinder the peace process.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Ultimately, Israelis and Palestinians need to have the political will to make the necessary concessions required in order to achieve a durable peace.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Given the difficulties and complexities of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, Singapore’s approach remains to be constructive, to be helpful, to support all efforts towards peace.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And we will continue to support international efforts to create the necessary conditions that will enable this peace process to begin again.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This was the key thrust of my remarks to the House on 2 July 2024.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: MFA will remain in close touch with all the Singaporeans who are e-registered in the region.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Our Embassy in Tel Aviv stands ready to provide consular assistance.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: All travellers to the Middle East are strongly encouraged to e-register with MFA and to please take precautions for personal safety.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In the Minister's view, is this a political, social or religious issue, or is it all three?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: If it is all three, how will we ensure in Singapore that this foreign issue does not impact our social compact and social cohesion?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The Member has mentioned that there may be political, social, religious dimensions.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: There will also be historical, cultural, geographical and economic dimensions to it.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: There is also, unfortunately, no quick and instant solution.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The main point that I think the Member is trying to raise is that given the complexities of the issue and the fact this is going to be so long-standing, how should Singapore and Singaporeans respond.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Given that we are multiracial, multilingual, multi-religious, we are an open city, we depend on free trade, we depend on the import of energy.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The point is that events far away can have profound impact on us.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: They can affect us economically, they can also affect our social, ethnic, religious harmony.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This is something which we need to be very, very mindful of.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Therein the point is as the Member had made – this is a foreign nation, this is something far away, but we should not under-estimate the impact that it can have on our society.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I think our paramount concern should be to maintain the unity and cohesion of all Singaporeans, that we are entitled to different opinions, different reactions even.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But above all, maintain our own domestic cohesion and collectivity.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And then, we can play our role as a responsible member of the international community, standing for peace, standing for international law, upholding principles, providing humanitarian assistance wherever it is needed.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And then, maintaining our communication channels open with all parties, even though some of these parties may be at war or doing things which, quite frankly, we find abhorrent.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: That is the position which I am trying to encourage us to maintain.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So far, you would have noticed that we have access to all parties.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I have been to Palestine, I have been to Israel, I have been to the Middle East.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I hope Members of this House will see that even in this dark hour, the unity of Singaporeans, the good will and generosity of Singaporeans, and the calm, measured, principled, consistent, diplomatic posture of Singapore is something which has been noticed and appreciated – certainly in the Middle East, but even on the international stage.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I note that the Minister shared that there is one Singaporean who is e-registered to travel to Lebanon and has decided to proceed.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I also further note that there are one travel notice and two travel advisories dated 17 April, 14 April and 7 February for the region.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The first supplementary question is, is the Ministry aware of how many Singaporeans remain in the immediate vicinity of the region, who are either registered or unregistered?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: And if the Ministry assesses the situation to become more serious, although this is rarely done, will MFA issue a stricter travel advisory for Singaporeans to completely avoid travel to the region?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I have already mentioned we have at least one in Lebanon.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: If that happens and you get into trouble, of course we would not leave you behind, but you are actually generating enormous work and concern, and sometimes even risk to the officers in MFA.
Unless there is really, really no choice, please do not go and please do not give us unnecessary extra work.
And I say this not because my officers are not willing to do the work – my officers are.

I would also want to make this point that MFA has got officers throughout the Middle East and I had never had a single officer come up to me and say, "There is a clear and present risk, please don't send me." So, I hope this House will also join me in expressing our appreciation and admiration for the Foreign Service Officers who put themselves on the frontlines, at risk, in order to represent us and to safeguard our interest and to help Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Foreign Minister had previously characterised the Israeli-Palestinian conflict as a family quarrel.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, I raise a question for the Foreign Minister, whether it is still appropriate to characterise the Israeli-Palestinian conflict as a "family quarrel", in light of the ICJ's advisory opinion?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I think we should never trivialise the tragedy that is unfolding there.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Maybe for the Member's edification, let me remind you of a speech which Senior Minister Lee made in November last year.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It is worth reading just one paragraph of that speech.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: He said, quote, "We are also watching closely, events in the Middle East.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The re-eruption of the Israel-Palestinian conflict has impacted Singapore.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The quarrel between the Israelis and Palestinians is not our quarrel, but it impacts our society.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But we must not let problems elsewhere widen fault lines in our society.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Let us indeed build on and strengthen our social harmony." So, that is the context, Mr Leong – do not let problems elsewhere widen our potential fault lines.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And none of us should seek to do that or take advantage of that for political point scoring.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: That is the real message to you and, indeed, it is a reminder to all of us.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Again, as I said, we can all have different perspectives and views.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We may be informed by religion, social conscience, our own interpretations of history.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But the paramount point here, let us not be divided.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And it is possible, and I hope in the fullness of time, it will be shown that Singapore is a mature, cohesive society that can deal with diversity and still rise up to the occasions, uphold principles, not take sides, be helpful, express the best part of our humanity and our compassion whilst understanding that life is complicated, especially in many other places.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I think if we can approach this with this spirit of humility and realism, we can be a useful exemplar to other parts of the world where these fault lines have not only cracked, but have led to enormous loss of life and, especially, innocent lives of civilians.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I think on that note, we are all completely united.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Given that the Minister has said that Singapore has access to many of the parties on all sides of the conflict, does Singapore have any plans to play some role to bring together the different sides, even in some small way?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Mr Gerald Giam accompanied me on my trip in March.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It is not a question of a venue for meeting or even offering good advice.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Both peoples occupying contested land are not going to leave and they will be a reality for each other till the end of time.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I think our excess is also because they know we are fair-minded people and that we are prepared to help wherever we can help.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But let us not overstep ourselves or assume that we have got a greater role than we can actually play.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: At the end, this is one little red dot, a shiny red dot, but we are still far away and many steps removed from them.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I would also remind you when we went and there were discussions about one state and two states.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And you will recall the conversation which I had with some senior people to say, "Well, if you want a one-state solution, your delegation must look like mine: multi-religious, multiracial and completely united, even across political boundaries".

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But I think you would have also got a sense from that trip that is very far removed from the reality in the Middle East, at least for now.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, again, I think this spirit of humility and consistency and upholding what is right, whilst maintaining the unity amidst our great diversity – I think that alone, is our contribution to show the world that it is possible to live in peace with your neighbour, with your brother.
